global_health.name: Global Health and Development
global_health.description: Saving lives and improving health in low-income countries

ea_frameworks.qalys: Quality-Adjusted Life Year: A measure of disease burden, with 1 QALY = 1 year of perfect health
ea_frameworks.dalys: Disability-Adjusted Life Year: A measure of overall disease burden, combining years of life lost and years lived with disability
ea_frameworks.expected_value: Expected Value: Probability × Impact, used for prioritizing interventions
ea_frameworks.triage: Triage: Prioritizing interventions based on urgency, scale, and neglectedness

faq.what_are_qualitative_measures: QALYs and DALYs are the most common quantitative measures in global health economics. QALYs measure quality-adjusted life years, while DALYs measure disability-adjusted life years - both help compare the impact of different interventions.
faq.how_do_i_choose_a_cause: The choice of cause area depends on your values, risk tolerance, and focus. Common considerations include: the scale of the problem (how many people are affected), the solvability of the problem (how effective solutions are), and the neglectedness of the area (how much funding/effort is already devoted to it).
faq.what_is_effective_altruism: Effective Altruism is a research-based approach to determining the most effective ways to benefit others. It combines compassion with evidence and reason to find the most effective solutions to the world's most pressing problems.
